## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There is no trial evidence yet. The starting network scored 0.000 on both seeds. With the default recipe, the budget is 131,072 steps at 4,096 steps per update, so the policy changes only 32 times while the learning rate falls to 0. The network already has a sensible structure for this task: 1x1 column encoders that see every layer of a column, 3x3 context convolutions, and heads that pool over each brick footprint, so landing height and flatness can be learned. So the most likely bottleneck is the recipe. Setting PPO epochs to 1 raises the budget to about 426k samples, and smaller batches give about 200 or more policy updates. Round 1 therefore runs two recipe points on the unchanged network and one deeper residual, dilated network that can see the whole grid, trained with the more promising recipe. If all three score 0, the recipe probably isn't the main problem.

### Round 2
Every trial scored 0 on dev, and training success was also 0 in every run. That held under three recipes (1 or 2 epochs, short or long horizon) and two trunks (plain and dilated residual), so on this evidence neither the recipe nor a deeper 2D trunk was the bottleneck. I think the gap is a reasoning step the network can't express. To place a brick correctly it must find the landing layer (the maximum height under the footprint) and check that every footprint cell at that layer is a missing target cell. A 2D trunk that mixes all layers into one feature map handles this conjunction poorly. My proposal is to compute features for each (layer, cell) pair: for each layer z, select that layer's channels and add the layer index as a coordinate. Shared 1x1 layers judge each cell at that layer, and pooling over the footprint then scores 'land here at z'. A logsumexp over layers turns this into anchor logits. A small 3x3 context layer is meant to catch overhang cases, where a correct-looking 1x1 brick would block a 2-cell brick that spans a gap.

### Round 3
All six trials scored exactly 0 on dev, and train success over the last 10% of training was also 0. That held across trunks (plain, dilated, per-layer), heads and recipes (1 or 2 epochs, short or long horizon). Seed noise cannot explain a total failure like this. Something all six share must be broken. Every head so far is fully convolutional: it puts the logit for anchor (y,x) at the action index the task describes. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. If the real action layout differs (transposed, flipped, a different anchor corner or a different type order), a local conv head cannot learn that remapping, and success stays at 0 whatever the trunk or recipe. This round tests heads that make no layout assumption: a dense head, a hybrid of the conv head plus a zero-initialised dense correction, and cross-attention from a learned per-action query, with the mask as input, to the cell tokens. If all three stay at 0, the layout idea is refuted and the cause is elsewhere (for example the reward or the DONE dynamics).

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored 0 on dev, and none built a single design exactly during training. That covers different recipes, trunks, per-layer scorers, dense heads and attention heads, so neither the network body nor the action layout looks like the bottleneck. A shared cause is more likely: the agent almost never chooses DONE. Every build overshoots, because any placement after completion adds extra cells, and the 33-placement limit never lines up with an exact finish. To succeed, the agent must choose DONE right after completion. But DONE is 1 logit among about 1,000 legal placements, so at the start it is sampled roughly 0.1% of the time. The entropy bonus over this large action space also pushes DONE's probability back toward about 1/1000. So the +1 bonus is never seen. All three candidates this round add a gated DONE head: p(DONE) comes from a sigmoid, and the placements share the remaining probability. Around that change they vary the entropy coefficient, the credit horizon and the trunk.
